title: Lord, How Secure My Conscience Was
description: Lord, How Secure My Conscience Was in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 115, headed “Conviction of sin by the law, Rom. 7. 8 9 14 24”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, how se-cure my con-science was, And felt no in-ward dread! I was a-live with-out the law, And thought my sins were dead.

lines: Lord, how secure my conscience was,
And felt no inward dread!
I was alive without the law,
And thought my sins were dead.
My hopes of heaven were firm and bright,
But since the precept came
With a convincing power and light,
I find how vile I am.
My guilt appear'd but small before,
Till terribly I saw
How perfect, holy, just, and pure,
Was thine eternal law.
Then felt my soul the heavy load,
My sins reviv'd again,
I had provok'd a dreadful God,
And all my hopes were slain.
I'm like a helpless captive sold
Under the power of sin;
I cannot do the good I would,
Nor keep my conscience clean.
My God, I cry with every breath
For some kind power to save,
To break the yoke of sin and death,
And thus redeem the slave.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
